newsitem.title: JAPAN: LME prices barely firmer in quiet Asian trade.
newsitem.headline: LME prices barely firmer in quiet Asian trade.

text.p: London Metal Exchange copper and aluminium prices were slightly firmer in quiet Asian trade on Wednesday after losses overnight.
One aluminium trader noted modest Japanese buying at the lower levels, although activity was light and he expected prices to remain in their recent ranges for the near term.
Sentiment toward the zinc market, which rose overnight despite losses in other metals, remained bullish.
A source at a leading Japanese trade house said the recent decline in LME warehouse stocks of zinc, which fell 13,025 tonnes on Tuesday, would continue to bolster the market.
He pegged a next upside target of $1,330 a tonne. LME three-month zinc ended Tuesday's afternoon kerb at $1,309.
At 0645 GMT, LME benchmark three-month copper was quoted at $2,362/67 a tonne, up slightly from $2,357/60 at 1900 GMT on Tuesday and $2,360 at the Tuesday afternoon kerb close.
Aluminium was quoted at $1,632/35 a tonne, up from $1,629/31 at 1900 GMT on Tuesday and $1,630.50 at the close of Tuesday's afternoon kerb.
